title: Traffic shaping for LLM rerankers - AB lab notes (working)
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a working lab notebook for designing and running cross-functional canaries and A/B experiments specifically targeting reranker components (post-generation reordering, reranking models, and heuristic fusion layers). Rerankers are high-leverage for quality and cost (they can reduce downstream token usage while changing perceived relevance), but they have brittle failure modes when upstream outputs drift. This doc collects practical traffic shaping patterns, instrumentation needs, rollback heuristics, and a lightweight protocol for product + infra + SRE to operate safe experiments.

Audience:
- Product managers owning ranking-related features
- ML engineers shipping reranker models
- Serving/runtime engineers who control traffic splits and proxies
- Observability/SRE owners who will declare KPIs and alerts

Quick summary of proposals (TL;DR):
- Use progressive interleaved exposure (PIE): start with deterministic sampling of 0.1% of users, then broaden via controlled interleaving so each user sees mixed exposures across sessions.
- Instrument per-session and per-request ranked-list signals: position-level CTR, satisfaction signals (explicit/implicit), generation cost delta (tokens saved), and diversity regressors.
- Define immediate safety gates (latency > 200ms p95, error rate > 0.5%, negative CTR delta > 5%) and medium-term quality gates (7-day retention uplift below threshold).
- Automate fallback to baseline model + traffic cool-down when any safety gate trips; require human review before re-escalation.

Traffic shaping patterns to consider:
1) Deterministic shard + bot-filtering start: route deterministic 0.1% of traffic by hashed user_id mod N to reranker variant. Exclude recognized bots and internal traffic.
2) Session-level interleaving: within a session, alternate baseline and variant requests on odd/even interactions to reduce per-session confounders. Use cookie/session tag to keep short-lived internal consistency.
3) Interleaved A/B with quota windows: maintain equal exposure within 24h rolling windows; implement traffic quotas at edge proxies to avoid burst artifacts.
4) Slice-first approach: prioritize slices by risk (low-risk = internal beta users, high-risk = new user cohorts). Do not expand slice until stability windows pass.
5) Cost-first safety shaping: cap variant exposure based on modeled token-savings vs error risk; if cost saving exceeds target but quality delta uncertain, keep exposure narrow and increase telemetry density.

Instrumentation and telemetry (must-haves):
- Per-request metadata: experiment_id, variant, model_version, user_cohort, request_latency_ms, downstream_tokens_consumed, upstream_tokens_generated, reranker_score_delta, position_changes (list as compact strings), request_trace_id
- Aggregates: p50/p95 latency for reranker-only path, error rate, model inference OOMs, average tokens saved per request, proportion of top-1 changes, top-3 churn rate
- User engagement metrics: click-through-by-position, dwell_time (30s/2m buckets), session-length post-rerank, downstream conversion (where applicable)
- Quality signals: manual annotations for sampled interactions (n=200/day target), automatic disagreement rate vs baseline (fraction of responses with immaterial conflict), toxicity/unsafe content false-positive/neg rates if applicable
- Health probes: synthetic traffic that exercises rare edge patterns (long prompt, high context length) at 10 qps across variants

Observation windows and decision cadence:
- Micro window (first 30m): watch for immediate catastrophes (latency spikes, 5xxs, OOMs). Auto-cooldown if safety gates hit.
- Short window (0–24h): monitor engagement deltas, token-savings, and early quality regressors. Stop expansion if negative short-term signals persist more than 3 sampling intervals.
- Medium window (3–7 days): retention and downstream conversion; require statistical power checks before labeling experiment success.
- Long window (14–30 days): product-level KPIs and long-tail failure modes.

Statistical and sampling guidance:
- Power targets: for relative CTR uplifts of 2–3% on baseline CTR ~2–5%, aim for at least 50k impressions per variant. Use sequential analysis and alpha spending to avoid repeated-testing fallacies.
- Use stratified sampling across primary slices (new vs returning users, mobile vs web, geo regions) to ensure balanced lifts and detect heterogenous effects early.

Rollout and rollback heuristics (operational):
- Immediate auto-rollback triggers (automated):
  * reranker latency p95 > 200ms above baseline for 15m
  * error rate (5xx or inference exceptions) > 0.5% absolute and 3x baseline
  * downstream safety classifier catching > 0.1% new incidents per 10k requests
- Soft-stop: pause expansion and notify on-call if negative CTR delta > 3% with p<0.05 on aggregated test slice in 24h window
- Manual gate: require explicit sign-off from PM + ML owner before expanding beyond 5% exposure or re-enabling after auto-rollback

Canary choreography (roles & runbook sketch):
- Pre-launch checklist (owners in parentheses):
  * Binary health tests + smoke-run on canary infra (Infra eng)
  * Telemetry wiring + dashboard skeleton (Observability)
  * Safety classifier thresholds validated on holdout (ML owner)
  * Sizing check / cost forecast for expected traffic (FinOps/Product)
  * Runbook and rollback playbook published to oncall page (SRE)
- Launch sequence:
  * T0: route 0.1% deterministic shard to variant, kick synthetic probe traffic, enable detailed logging sampling (1:1 for first hour)
  * T+30m: evaluate micro-window metrics; auto-cooldown on infra issues
  * T+6h: if stable, expand to 1% and switch logging to 1:10 sampling while keeping important histograms at full fidelity
  * T+24h: run initial statistical checks for engagement and safety; if pass, expand to 5% with manual sign-off for 24–72h observation

Open questions (to resolve before wider adoption):
- How do we consistently measure "tokens saved" when downstream orchestration may reissue requests (double counting risk)? Action: infra + runtime to add a unique request lineage id.
- For multi-variant studies that change reranker architecture and upstream prompt conditioning simultaneously, what's the recommended randomization hierarchy? Action: prefer orthogonalization where reranker changes are kept separate from prompt/decoder experiments.
- What SLA should we expose for reranker latency p95 as a function of sequence length? Action: propose latency SLO buckets (short/medium/long) and map to cost allowances in Optimize.

Example checklist for an individual experiment (copyable):
- [ ] Create experiment entry in experiments registry with hypothesis and primary metric (PM)
- [ ] Link GH PR for model and ruleset changes
- [ ] Create dashboard with these panels: latency, error rate, tokens saved, CTR by pos, manual annotation queue
- [ ] Define slices and sampling strategy (list of cohorts)
- [ ] Pre-deploy to staging and run synthetic suite for 2h
- [ ] Launch to 0.1% deterministic shard + enable synthetic probes
- [ ] Observe 30m micro-window and update runbook notes
- [ ] Expand cadence (0.1->1->5) only on green checks and sign-offs

Notes to self / working fragments:
- Felt need for a small library that maps experiment telemetry to the rollout decision matrix (input: metric stream, outputs: go/no-go flags + recommended expansion step). Could be a repo under experiments/auto-guardrails.
- Short term: make a templated dashboard and a templated PR checklist to reduce human error across teams.
- Consider a "risky-slice" tag that gates scheduling in traffic router to avoid simultaneous risky experiments across multiple features for the same user cohort.

Next actions (owners assigned):
- Marco: prototype lineage id for token accounting (ETA 2 weeks)
- Riley: build dashboard template and share with product-console (ETA 1 week)
- Sofia: draft formal safety-gate thresholds and add to SRE runbook (ETA 10 days)
- Aisha: consolidate this doc into a short one-pager for exec-readiness after first successful lab run (ETA after first passing canary)

Last edited notes: iterative, patchy style — this is intentionally a working lab notebook. If you are reading and want edit rights ping me in #prod-console.

End of doc.
